questions.question: An agent sells a turbo cooker with a marked price of ₹6,370 at a discount of 50%. What is the selling price (in ₹) of the turbo cooker?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A discount of 50% means the selling price is exactly half of the marked price.

SP = MP ÷ 2

SP = 6370 ÷ 2

SP = 3185

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,185.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 MP = ₹6,370

 
• 
 − 50% Discount

 
 SP = ?

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹6,370

Discount = 50%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount Amount

Discount Amount = (Discount% ÷ 100) × MP

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount Amount = (50 ÷ 100) × 6370

⇒ Discount Amount = 1/2 × 6370

⇒ Discount Amount = 3185

⇒ SP = 6370 − 3185

⇒ SP = 3185

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,185.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price vs Cost Price

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP), whereas Profit and Loss are calculated on the Cost Price (CP).

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts d₁% and d₂% are offered, the effective discount percentage is given by: [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 100]%.

Selling Price Relation

SP can be expressed relative to both MP and CP: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

questions.question: P and Q together can fill a cistern with water in 15 hours. If P alone can fill the cistern with water in 40 hours, then in how many hours will Q alone fill one-fourth of the same cistern with water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity of the cistern = LCM(15, 40) = 120 units.

Efficiency of (P + Q) = 120 ÷ 15 = 8 units/hour, and Efficiency of P = 120 ÷ 40 = 3 units/hour.

Efficiency of Q = 8 − 3 = 5 units/hour.

Time required for Q alone to fill 1/4th of the cistern = (120 ÷ 4) ÷ 5 = 30 ÷ 5 = 6 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P and Q together to fill the cistern = 15 hours

Time taken by P alone to fill the cistern = 40 hours

**Concept Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time Taken

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Hours**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 P + Q
 15
 120
 8
 
 

 P
 40
 3
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of Q = Efficiency of (P + Q) − Efficiency of P

⇒ Efficiency of Q = 8 − 3 = 5 units/hour

⇒ Total work to fill one-fourth of the cistern = 120 × (1/4) = 30 units

⇒ Time taken by Q alone = Work to be done ÷ Efficiency of Q

⇒ Time taken by Q alone = 30 ÷ 5 = 6 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Rule

Inlet pipes that fill the tank are considered to have a positive efficiency, while outlet pipes (or leaks) that empty the tank are considered to have a negative efficiency.

Fractional Work Principle

If an entire work is completed in *x* hours, then 1/n of the same work will directly take *x* ÷ n hours, provided the efficiency remains constant.

Work and Wages

When multiple people work together, the wages are divided precisely in the ratio of the total work individually completed. If they start and finish together, wages are shared in the ratio of their efficiencies.

questions.question: {The value of } ((a² - b²)³ + (b² - c²)³ + (c² - a²)³)/((a - b)³ + (b - c)³ + (c - a)³) { is:}
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use identity: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)

So numerator = (a − b)³(a + b)³ + cyclic terms

Apply identity: x³ + y³ + z³ = 3xyz when x + y + z = 0

Here (a − b) + (b − c) + (c − a) = 0 ⇒ numerator = 3(a − b)(b − c)(c − a)(a + b)(b + c)(c + a)

Denominator = 3(a − b)(b − c)(c − a)

**∴ Answer = (a + b)(b + c)(c + a)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

[(a² − b²)³ + (b² − c²)³ + (c² − a²)³] ÷ [(a − b)³ + (b − c)³ + (c − a)³]

**Formula used:**

a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc when a + b + c = 0

**Calculation:**

⇒ (a² − b²) = (a − b)(a + b)

⇒ Numerator = (a − b)³(a + b)³ + (b − c)³(b + c)³ + (c − a)³(c + a)³

⇒ Let x = (a − b), y = (b − c), z = (c − a)

⇒ x + y + z = 0

⇒ Numerator = 3xyz (a + b)(b + c)(c + a)

⇒ Denominator = x³ + y³ + z³ = 3xyz

⇒ Required value = [3xyz (a + b)(b + c)(c + a)] ÷ [3xyz]

⇒ = (a + b)(b + c)(c + a)

**∴ The correct answer is (a + b)(b + c)(c + a).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Cubes Identity

If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc

Difference of Squares

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)

Cyclic Expressions

Expressions repeating in pattern (a,b,c) can often be simplified using symmetry

Common Factor Cancellation

If same factor appears in numerator and denominator, it can be cancelled directly

questions.question: Simplify: 86 − (− 16) × (− 8 − 20 − 18) ÷ [1 × {10 + (− 2) × (− 3)}]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the brackets using the BODMAS rule directly.

Inner bracket: (−8 − 20 − 18) = −46

Square bracket: [1 × {10 + (−2) × (−3)}] = [1 × {10 + 6}] = 16

Remaining expression: 86 − (−16) × (−46) ÷ 16

⇒ 86 − (736 ÷ 16) = 86 − 46 = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: 86 − (−16) × (−8 − 20 − 18) ÷ [1 × {10 + (−2) × (−3)}]

**Method Used:**

BODMAS Rule (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 86 − (−16) × (−8 − 20 − 18) ÷ [1 × {10 + (−2) × (−3)}]

⇒ 86 − (−16) × (−46) ÷ [1 × {10 + 6}]

⇒ 86 − (−16) × (−46) ÷ [1 × 16]

⇒ 86 − (−16) × (−46) ÷ 16

⇒ 86 − 736 ÷ 16

⇒ 86 − 46

⇒ 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It stands for Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction. Expressions are simplified in this strict sequential order.

Order of Brackets

Always solve brackets in the order: Line bracket (bar), Simple brackets (), Curly brackets {}, and finally Square brackets [].

Sign Multiplication Rules

When multiplying numbers with the same signs, the result is positive (− × − = +). When multiplying numbers with different signs, the result is negative (+ × − = −).
</p

questions.question: The volume (in m³) of a cube with edges of 31 m is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The unit digit of the given edge length 31 is 1.

The volume of a cube is calculated by cubing its edge length (31 × 31 × 31).

Therefore, the unit digit of the resulting volume must also be 1 × 1 × 1 = 1.

Looking at the given options, only 29791 ends with the digit 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 29791 m³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Side length of the cube (a) = 31 m

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cube = a³

**Calculation:**

⇒ Volume = 31 × 31 × 31

⇒ Volume = 961 × 31

⇒ Volume = 29791

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cube

The total surface area is the sum of the areas of all 6 faces. The formula is: 6 × a².

Diagonal of a Cube

Volume of a Cuboid

questions.question: Sunita, Javed, and Rani invest ₹13,90,000, ₹4,70,000, and ₹15,40,000, respectively, to start a business. If the profit at the end of the year is ₹4,50,500, then what is the share of Rani in the profit?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit ratio = Ratio of investments (since the investment time is equal for all).

Sunita : Javed : Rani = 1390000 : 470000 : 1540000 = 139 : 47 : 154

Total profit ratio parts = 139 + 47 + 154 = 340 parts.

Rani's share in profit = (154 ÷ 340) × 450500 = 154 × 1325 = 204050.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,04,050.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sunita's Investment = ₹13,90,000

Javed's Investment = ₹4,70,000

Rani's Investment = ₹15,40,000

Total Profit at the end of the year = ₹4,50,500

**Formula Used:**

When the time period is constant for all investors, the Profit Ratio is directly proportional to the Ratio of Investment.

 139 parts 47 parts 154 parts 
• Sunita Javed Rani Investment Ratio Comparison 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit Ratio (Sunita : Javed : Rani) = 1390000 : 470000 : 1540000

⇒ Profit Ratio = 139 : 47 : 154

⇒ Total Ratio Parts = 139 + 47 + 154 = 340 parts

⇒ Rani's share = (Rani's ratio parts ÷ Total ratio parts) × Total Profit

⇒ Rani's share = (154 ÷ 340) × 450500

⇒ Rani's share = 154 × (450500 ÷ 340)

⇒ Rani's share = 154 × 1325

⇒ Rani's share = ₹2,04,050

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,04,050.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Different Time Periods

If partners invest their capitals for different durations, the profit ratio is calculated as (Capital₁ × Time₁) : (Capital₂ × Time₂).

Sleeping vs Working Partner

A working partner receives a fixed salary or a certain percentage of profit for managing the business operations. The remaining profit is then distributed among all partners in the ratio of their investments.

Joining Mid-way

When a partner joins the business after a few months, their time period of investment is calculated strictly from the date of joining to the end of the accounting year.

questions.question: The distance between points A and B is 663 km. Amit travels from A to B at 131 km/hr and returns at 24 km/hr. Calculate his average speed for the entire journey (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the distance traveled is the same for two parts of a journey, the exact distance is not needed.

Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

⇒ Average Speed = (2 × 131 × 24) ÷ (131 + 24)

⇒ Average Speed = 6288 ÷ 155

⇒ Average Speed ≈ 40.567 km/hr ≈ 40.57 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 40.57 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 A B 
• Distance = 663 km 
• 
 Speed = 131 km/hr 
• 
 Speed = 24 km/hr 

**Given:**

Distance from A to B (D) = 663 km

Speed from A to B (S₁) = 131 km/hr

Speed from B to A (S₂) = 24 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 663 + 663 = 1326 km

⇒ Total Time = (663 ÷ 131) + (663 ÷ 24)

⇒ Total Time = 663 × (1/131 + 1/24)

⇒ Total Time = 663 × [(24 + 131) ÷ (131 × 24)] = 663 × (155 ÷ 3144) hr

⇒ Average Speed = 1326 ÷ [663 × (155 ÷ 3144)]

⇒ Average Speed = (1326 × 3144) ÷ (663 × 155)

⇒ Average Speed = 2 × (3144 ÷ 155)

⇒ Average Speed = 6288 ÷ 155

⇒ Average Speed = 40.5677... ≈ 40.57 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 40.57 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Two Equal Distances

When a person covers two equal consecutive distances or travels back and forth between two points at speeds x and y, the average speed formula is (2xy) ÷ (x + y). The actual distance measurement is redundant.

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

If a journey consists of three equal distances covered at speeds x, y, and z, the average speed is directly given by (3xyz) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Average Speed for Unequal Distances

For unequal distances D₁, D₂... covered at speeds S₁, S₂... the general formula is Average Speed = (D₁ + D₂ + ...) ÷ (D₁/S₁ + D₂/S₂ + ...).

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 74 and their difference is 12. Find the product of the two numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Larger number = (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2 = (74 + 12) ÷ 2 = 43

Smaller number = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2 = (74 − 12) ÷ 2 = 31

Product of the numbers = 43 × 31 = 1333

**∴ The correct answer is 1333.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of two numbers (x + y) = 74

Difference of two numbers (x − y) = 12

**Formula Used:**

4xy = (x + y)² − (x − y)²

**Calculations:**

⇒ 4xy = 74² − 12²

⇒ 4xy = (74 + 12) × (74 − 12)

⇒ 4xy = 86 × 62

⇒ xy = (86 × 62) ÷ 4

⇒ xy = 43 × 31 = 1333

**∴ The correct answer is 1333.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity for Sum of Squares

(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)

Difference of Squares

a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
</p

questions.question: In a quadrilateral EFGH, ∠E = 52° and ∠F = 37°. The bisectors of ∠G and ∠H meet at X. What is the measure of ∠HXG?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In any quadrilateral, the angle formed by the intersection of the angle bisectors of two adjacent angles is half the sum of the remaining two interior angles.

⇒ ∠HXG = (∠E + ∠F) ÷ 2

⇒ ∠HXG = (52° + 37°) ÷ 2

⇒ ∠HXG = 89° ÷ 2 = 44.5°

**∴ The correct answer is 44.5°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

∠E = 52°

∠F = 37°

X is the intersection point of the angle bisectors of ∠G and ∠H.

 
 

 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 E
 F
 G
 H
 X
 
 
 52°
 37°
 ?

**Formula Used:**

Sum of all interior angles of a quadrilateral = 360°

Sum of all interior angles of a triangle = 180°

**Calculations:**

In quadrilateral EFGH,

⇒ ∠E + ∠F + ∠G + ∠H = 360°

⇒ 52° + 37° + ∠G + ∠H = 360°

⇒ 89° + ∠G + ∠H = 360°

⇒ ∠G + ∠H = 360° − 89°

⇒ ∠G + ∠H = 271°

Since XG and XH are the respective angle bisectors of ∠G and ∠H,

⇒ ∠HGX = ∠G ÷ 2

⇒ ∠GHX = ∠H ÷ 2

Now, considering triangle HXG,

⇒ ∠HXG + ∠HGX + ∠GHX = 180°

⇒ ∠HXG + (∠G ÷ 2) + (∠H ÷ 2) = 180°

⇒ ∠HXG + (∠G + ∠H) ÷ 2 = 180°

⇒ ∠HXG + (271° ÷ 2) = 180°

⇒ ∠HXG + 135.5° = 180°

⇒ ∠HXG = 180° − 135.5°

⇒ ∠HXG = 44.5°

**∴ The correct answer is 44.5°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle Sum Property of a Quadrilateral

The sum of the interior angles of any simple quadrilateral is always 360°. This fundamental property applies because a quadrilateral can be divided into two separate triangles along a diagonal.

Incentre of a Triangle

When the angle bisectors of the two base angles of a triangle intersect at a point (the incentre), the angle formed at the intersection is equal to 90° + (∠opposite base angle ÷ 2).

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

A cyclic quadrilateral is one in which all four vertices lie precisely on the circumference of a single circle. In such a shape, the sum of any pair of opposite interior angles is strictly supplementary (adding to 180°).
</p

questions.question: The cost price of a dress is ₹1,600. The shopkeeper makes a profit of 20% on selling it. If he offers a discount of 25% at the time of sale, find the marked price (in ₹).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct ratio method relating Marked Price (MP) and Cost Price (CP):

MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%)

⇒ MP ÷ 1600 = (100 + 20) ÷ (100 − 25)

⇒ MP = 1600 × (120 ÷ 75) = 1600 × (8 ÷ 5)

⇒ MP = 320 × 8 = 2560

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2560.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹1,600

Profit = 20%

Discount = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

Marked Price (MP) = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − Discount%)

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 CP
 ₹1600
 
 
 SP
 ₹1920
 
 
 MP
 ₹2560

 

 + 20% Profit
 
 

 − 25% Discount

 Relation: MP ÷ CP = (100 + P%) ÷ (100 − D%)

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 1600 × (100 + 20) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 1600 × 120 ÷ 100 = 1600 × 1.2 = ₹1920

⇒ The shopkeeper gives a 25% discount on the Marked Price (MP).

⇒ SP = MP × (100 − 25) ÷ 100

⇒ 1920 = MP × 75 ÷ 100

⇒ 1920 = MP × (3 ÷ 4)

⇒ MP = 1920 × 4 ÷ 3 = 640 × 4

⇒ MP = ₹2560

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2560.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct CP to MP Formula

A very useful formula relating Cost Price, Marked Price, Profit% and Discount% is: CP × (100 + Profit%) = MP × (100 − Discount%). This bypasses the need to calculate Selling Price entirely.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is given by the formula: [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer sells goods at CP but uses a false weight, the actual profit percentage is calculated as: [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells 10 identical watches for ₹10,500, which is the cost price of 8 watches. Find his loss percentage.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

10 watches SP = cost of 8 watches

So CP:SP ratio = 10 : 8

Loss = 2 parts out of 10

Loss% = (2 ÷ 10) × 100

**∴ Answer = 20%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling price of 10 watches = ₹10500

Cost price of 8 watches = ₹10500

**Formula used:**

Loss % = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ CP of 1 watch = 10500 ÷ 8 = 1312.5

⇒ SP of 1 watch = 10500 ÷ 10 = 1050

⇒ Loss per watch = 1312.5 − 1050 = 262.5

⇒ Loss % = (262.5 ÷ 1312.5) × 100

⇒ Loss % = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Formula

Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100 and Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

Basic Relation

Loss = CP − SP and Profit = SP − CP

Ratio Method

If CP:SP is known, loss or profit can be found directly using ratio difference

Unitary Method

Find cost and selling price per unit first, then calculate total profit or loss

questions.question: (1)/(30) { is what percentage of } (2)/(20) { (rounded off to two decimal places)?}

questions.question:
What is the mode of the following data?

53, 53, 40, 49, 50, 48, 53, 50, 41, 40, 53, 45, 40, 47, 43, 52, 51, 42, 51, 53
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The mode of a dataset is simply the observation that appears the most frequently.

By quickly scanning the given list of numbers, we can see that 53 appears 5 times, which is more than any other number.

**∴ The correct answer is 53.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Data: 53, 53, 40, 49, 50, 48, 53, 50, 41, 40, 53, 45, 40, 47, 43, 52, 51, 42, 51, 53

**Concept Used:**

Mode = The value that has the highest frequency in a given set of data.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let us arrange the data in ascending order to easily count the frequencies:

⇒ 40, 40, 40, 41, 42, 43, 45, 47, 48, 49, 50, 50, 51, 51, 52, 53, 53, 53, 53, 53

⇒ Frequency of 40 = 3

⇒ Frequency of 50 = 2

⇒ Frequency of 51 = 2

⇒ Frequency of 53 = 5

⇒ All other numbers have a frequency of 1.

⇒ Since 53 has the maximum frequency (it appears 5 times), it is the mode of the given data.

**∴ The correct answer is 53.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean

The mean is the arithmetic average of a dataset, calculated by dividing the sum of all observations by the total number of observations.

Median

The median is the middlemost value of a dataset when arranged in ascending or descending order. If the number of terms is even, it is the average of the two middle terms.

Empirical Relationship

The relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode for a moderately skewed distribution is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Range

The range is the difference between the highest (maximum) and lowest (minimum) values in a dataset.

questions.question: Two pipes, F and M, can fill a cistern in 25 minutes and 30 minutes, respectively. If both pipes are opened together, after how many minutes should pipe F be closed so that the cistern is completely filled in 15 minutes?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Total Work = LCM(25, 30) = 150 units.

Efficiency of F = 150 ÷ 25 = 6 units/min and Efficiency of M = 150 ÷ 30 = 5 units/min.

M works for full 15 min ⇒ Work done by M = 5 × 15 = 75 units.

Remaining work = 150 − 75 = 75 units.

Time taken by F = 75 ÷ 6 = 12.5 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by F = 25 minutes

Time taken by M = 30 minutes

Total time = 15 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of Time Taken

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 F

 150 ÷ 25 = 6

 150 ÷ 30 = 5
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of F = 6 units/min

⇒ Efficiency of M = 5 units/min

⇒ Work done by M in 15 minutes = 5 × 15 = 75 units

⇒ Remaining work = 150 − 75 = 75 units

⇒ Time taken by F = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of F

⇒ Time taken by F = 75 ÷ 6 = 12.5 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question: A tower stands vertically on the ground. From a point on the ground which is 29.6 m away from the foot of the tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is found to be 45°. Find the height of the tower.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a right-angled triangle, if the angle of elevation is 45°, the other acute angle is also 45°.

This forms an isosceles right-angled triangle where the perpendicular height is exactly equal to the base distance.

Since the base distance is 29.6 m, the height of the tower is directly 29.6 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 29.6 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance of the point from the foot of the tower (BC) = 29.6 m

Angle of elevation to the top of the tower (θ) = 45°

 
• 
 
 
 A (Top) B (Foot) C 45° 29.6 m h = ? 

**Formula Used:**

In a right-angled triangle, tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

**Calculations:**

Let the height of the tower be AB = h.

⇒ tan 45° = AB ÷ BC

⇒ 1 = h ÷ 29.6

⇒ h = 29.6

**∴ The correct answer is 29.6 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when viewing an object placed above the horizontal level.

Angle of Depression

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when viewing an object placed below the horizontal level.

Common Trigonometric Values

tan 30° = 1 ÷ √3 | tan 45° = 1 | tan 60° = √3

Ratio of Sides for Common Angles

For a 45°-45°-90° right triangle, the sides opposite to the angles are always in the ratio 1 : 1 : √2.

questions.question: If A6B59 is exactly divisible by 9, then find the least possible value of (A²+2B) .
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of digits of A6B59 = A + 6 + B + 5 + 9 = A + B + 20.

For divisibility by 9, the sum must be a multiple of 9 ⇒ A + B + 20 = 27 ⇒ A + B = 7.

To minimize A² + 2B, we must choose the smallest positive integer for A. Thus, A = 1 and B = 6.

Minimum value = 1² + 2 × 6 = 1 + 12 = 13.

**∴ The correct answer is 13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number = A6B59, which is exactly divisible by 9.

**Formula Used:**

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 9.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of digits = A + 6 + B + 5 + 9

⇒ Sum of digits = A + B + 20

⇒ The possible multiples of 9 greater than 20 are 27 and 36.

⇒ Case 1: A + B + 20 = 27 ⇒ A + B = 7

⇒ Case 2: A + B + 20 = 36 ⇒ A + B = 16

⇒ We need the least possible value of (A² + 2B). Since A is squared, smaller values of A will yield smaller results.

⇒ In Case 1 (A + B = 7), testing possible values for A and B (with A ≥ 1):

⇒ If A = 1, B = 6 ⇒ A² + 2B = 1² + 2 × 6 = 13

⇒ If A = 2, B = 5 ⇒ A² + 2B = 2² + 2 × 5 = 14

⇒ If A = 3, B = 4 ⇒ A² + 2B = 3² + 2 × 4 = 17

⇒ The value of (A² + 2B) increases as A increases.

⇒ In Case 2 (A + B = 16), the values will be much larger (e.g., A = 7, B = 9 yields 49 + 18 = 67).

⇒ Therefore, the least possible value is obtained when A = 1 and B = 6.

⇒ Least value = 13

**∴ The correct answer is 13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of all its digits is a multiple of 3.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of all its digits is a multiple of 9.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

questions.question: A metallic sphere of unknown radius is melted and recast into 64 smaller spherical balls. During the recasting process, 20% of the total metal is lost as waste. If the total volume of the 64 smaller spheres after the loss is 10,752 cm³, determine the radius (rounded off to the nearest integer) of the original sphere. (Use pi = 3.14 )
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Final volume = 10752 cm³ represents 80% of original metal

Original volume = 10752 ÷ 0.8 = 13440 cm³

Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³

13440 = (4/3) × 3.14 × r³

r³ ≈ 3213

**∴ r ≈ 15 cm**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total volume of 64 small spheres after loss = 10752 cm³

Loss = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³

**Calculation:**

⇒ Remaining metal = 80% of original

⇒ Original volume = 10752 ÷ 0.8 = 13440 cm³

⇒ Using formula:

⇒ 13440 = (4/3) × 3.14 × r³

⇒ 13440 = 4.1867 × r³

⇒ r³ = 13440 ÷ 4.1867 ≈ 3210

⇒ r ≈ ∛3210 ≈ 15 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 15 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Sphere

Volume = (4/3)πr³

Percentage Loss

If x% is lost, remaining = (100 − x)% of original

Recasting Concept

Total volume is conserved except for loss during melting

questions.question: The ratio of three numbers is 12:14:4. If 25% of the first number is 18, then what would 30% of the difference between the third and second numbers be?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

25% of first = 18 ⇒ first = 72

Ratio 12 : 14 : 4 ⇒ 1 part = 72 ÷ 12 = 6

Second = 14 × 6 = 84, Third = 4 × 6 = 24

Difference = 84 − 24 = 60

30% of 60 = 18

**∴ Answer = 18**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of numbers = 12 : 14 : 4

25% of first number = 18

**Formula used:**

Number = Ratio part × common multiplier

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let first number = 12x

⇒ 25% of 12x = 18

⇒ 3x = 18

⇒ x = 6

⇒ First = 12x = 72

⇒ Second = 14x = 84

⇒ Third = 4x = 24

⇒ Difference (second − third) = 84 − 24 = 60

⇒ Required = 30% of 60 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Method

Numbers in ratio are expressed as multiples of a common variable x.

Percentage Conversion

25% = 1/4 and 30% = 3/10 helps simplify calculations quickly.

Difference Concept

Always take positive difference when order is not fixed.

questions.question: The ratio of the ages of a wife and husband is 6 : 7 at present. If the sum of their ages after 20 years from now is 92, then find their present ages (in years), respectively.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let present ages = 6x and 7x

After 20 years ⇒ (6x+20) + (7x+20) = 92

13x + 40 = 92 ⇒ 13x = 52

x = 4

**∴ Ages = 24 years and 28 years**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of wife : husband = 6 : 7

Sum after 20 years = 92

**Formula used:**

Future age = Present age + years

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let present ages be 6x and 7x

⇒ After 20 years: (6x + 20) and (7x + 20)

⇒ Sum = (6x + 20) + (7x + 20)

⇒ 13x + 40 = 92

⇒ 13x = 52

⇒ x = 4

⇒ Wife's age = 6x = 24

⇒ Husband's age = 7x = 28

**∴ The correct answer is 24 years and 28 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Age Ratio Concept

Ages in ratio can be written as multiples of a common variable x.

Future Age Formula

Future age = Present age + number of years.

Linear Equation

Form equation using given condition and solve for unknown variable.

questions.question: If the HCF of three numbers is 23 and they are in the ratio 1:2:3, then the numbers are:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the ratio of numbers is given as a : b : c and their HCF is H, the numbers are directly given by a × H, b × H, and c × H.

Given ratio = 1 : 2 : 3 and HCF = 23.

First number = 1 × 23 = 23

Second number = 2 × 23 = 46

Third number = 3 × 23 = 69

**∴ The correct answer is 23, 46, 69.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of the three numbers = 1 : 2 : 3

Highest Common Factor (HCF) = 23

**Concept Used:**

When numbers are in a given ratio, they can be represented as multiples of a common variable x, where x exactly represents the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of those numbers.

 Ratio to Numbers Conversion
 
 I
 
 1x
 → 1 × 23 = 23

 II
 
 2x
 → 2 × 23 = 46

 III
 
 3x
 → 3 × 23 = 69

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the three numbers be 1x, 2x, and 3x respectively.

⇒ The common factor for x, 2x, and 3x is x, which means their HCF is x.

⇒ We are given that the HCF is 23, therefore x = 23.

⇒ Substituting x = 23 into the assumed numbers:

⇒ First number = 1 × 23 = 23

⇒ Second number = 2 × 23 = 46

⇒ Third number = 3 × 23 = 69

⇒ The three numbers are 23, 46, and 69.

**∴ The correct answer is 23, 46, 69.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between Numbers, HCF and LCM

For any two given numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is identically equal to the product of their HCF and LCM. Formula: A × B = HCF × LCM. Note: This rule is only applicable to exactly two numbers.

HCF of Co-prime numbers

Two numbers are considered co-prime if their Highest Common Factor (HCF) is exactly 1. The LCM of any two such co-prime numbers is simply their product.

HCF and LCM of Fractions

HCF of fractions = (HCF of numerators) ÷ (LCM of denominators). Similarly, LCM of fractions = (LCM of numerators) ÷ (HCF of denominators).

questions.question: The amount on a sum of ₹5,200 at 20% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, in 2 years will be:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective compound interest rate for 2 years at 20% = 20 + 20 + (20 × 20) ÷ 100 = 44%

Total Amount = Principal (100%) + Interest (44%) = 144% of Principal

⇒ Amount = 144% of 5200

⇒ Amount = 1.44 × 5200 = 7488

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,488.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹5,200

Rate (R) = 20% per annum

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R ÷ 100)T

 
 
• Start Year 1 Year 2 ₹5,200 ₹6,240 ₹7,488 
 
 + 20% + 20% Final Amount = ₹7,488 

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 5200 × (1 + 20 ÷ 100)²

⇒ A = 5200 × (1 + 1 ÷ 5)²

⇒ A = 5200 × (6 ÷ 5)²

⇒ A = 5200 × (36 ÷ 25)

⇒ A = 208 × 36

⇒ A = 7488

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,488.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of Compound Interest

For 2 years, the effective CI rate can be found directly using the successive percentage change formula: R + R + (R² ÷ 100)%.

Difference between CI and SI

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years on a given principal is calculated as: D = P(R ÷ 100)².

Half-yearly Compounding

When compound interest is calculated half-yearly, the annual rate of interest is halved (R ÷ 2) and the number of compounding time periods is doubled (2T).

questions.question: Two trains, Train A and Train B, are traveling towards each other on parallel tracks. Train A is 150 meters long and moves at a speed of 72 km/h. Train B is 100 meters long and moves at a speed of 54 km/h. How much time (rounded off to two decimal places) will it take for Train A to completely pass Train B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Opposite direction ⇒ relative speed = sum

72 km/hr = 20 m/s, 54 km/hr = 15 m/s

Relative speed = 20 + 15 = 35 m/s

Total distance = 150 + 100 = 250 m

Time = 250 ÷ 35 ≈ 7.14 sec

**∴ Answer = 7.14 seconds**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of Train A = 150 m, Speed = 72 km/hr

Length of Train B = 100 m, Speed = 54 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Time = Total distance ÷ Relative speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Convert speeds into m/s

⇒ 72 km/hr = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s

⇒ 54 km/hr = 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s

⇒ Relative speed (opposite direction) = 20 + 15 = 35 m/s

⇒ Total distance = 150 + 100 = 250 m

⇒ Time = 250 ÷ 35

⇒ Time ≈ 7.14 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 7.14 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When objects move in opposite directions, relative speed = sum of speeds.

Train Crossing Concept

Total distance covered = sum of lengths when crossing each other.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18.
